typedef struct mz_zip_file_s {
    uint16_t version_madeby;     /* version made by */
    uint16_t version_needed;     /* version needed to extract */
    uint16_t flag;               /* general purpose bit flag */
    uint16_t compression_method; /* compression method */
    time_t modified_date;        /* last modified date in unix time */
    time_t accessed_date;        /* last accessed date in unix time */
    time_t creation_date;        /* creation date in unix time */
    uint32_t crc;                /* crc-32 */
    int64_t compressed_size;     /* compressed size */
    int64_t uncompressed_size;   /* uncompressed size */
    uint16_t filename_size;      /* filename length */
    uint16_t extrafield_size;    /* extra field length */
    uint16_t comment_size;       /* file comment length */
    uint32_t disk_number;        /* disk number start */
    int64_t disk_offset;         /* relative offset of local header */
    uint16_t internal_fa;        /* internal file attributes */
    uint32_t external_fa;        /* external file attributes */
    const char *filename;        /* filename utf8 null-terminated string */
    const uint8_t *extrafield;   /* extrafield data */
    const char *comment;         /* comment utf8 null-terminated string */
    const char *linkname;        /* sym-link filename utf8 null-terminated string */
    uint16_t zip64;              /* zip64 extension mode */
    uint16_t aes_version;        /* winzip aes extension if not 0 */
    uint8_t aes_strength;        /* winzip aes encryption strength */
    uint16_t pk_verify;          /* pkware encryption verifier */
} mz_zip_file, mz_zip_entry;
objects.description: File metadata and per-entry information used by minizip-ng. Holds central/local header fields, sizes, timestamps, attributes, and pointers to associated name/extra/comment/link strings. mz_zip_entry is an alias to the same struct type. Some pointer members reference external memory; lifetimes are managed by the zip handle functions. Unknowns: ownership semantics of filename/extrafield/comment/linkname are not explicitly documented here.

functions.description: Destroys and frees a raw stream object created by mz_stream_raw_create, setting the caller's pointer to NULL.
requirements: stream must be non-null and *stream must be a stream previously created by mz_stream_raw_create (or compatible)

functions.name: mz_zip_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ZIP handle used to open/read/write ZIP archives. Use the returned handle with other mz_zip_* APIs, and free it with mz_zip_delete when finished.
requirements: Call mz_zip_delete to release the returned handle when no longer needed.
The returned pointer must be passed as the handle parameter to other mz_zip_* functions.
Thread-safety and allocation failure behavior are unknown; handle may be NULL on failure (not documented).

functions.name: mz_zip_delete
functions.description: Releases and destroys a ZIP handle created by mz_zip_create. Accepts a pointer to the handle so the function can invalidate it after deletion.
requirements: handle must not be NULL.
*handle must be a handle returned by mz_zip_create.
After successful deletion, *handle may be set to NULL by the function; do not use the handle afterwards.
Close any open ZIP (mz_zip_close) or open entry (mz_zip_entry_*_close) before deleting the handle to avoid undefined behavior (not explicitly documented but typical).

functions.name: mz_zip_open
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive on the provided stream with the specified mode (e.g., read/write/create, library-specific). This prepares the handle for ZIP operations. Comment notes: "Create a zip file, no delete file in zip functionality."
requirements: handle must be a valid handle from mz_zip_create.
stream must be a valid stream object compatible with minizip-ng (type unspecified here).
mode must be a valid library-defined open mode; exact values are not documented in this header.
Must be called before any entry navigation or read/write operations.
Return value should be checked for success before proceeding.

functions.name: mz_zip_close
functions.description: Closes the ZIP archive associated with the handle, flushing pending changes and releasing resources tied to the open archive (but not deleting the handle object itself).
requirements: handle must be a valid handle opened with mz_zip_open.
Do not perform entry operations after closing until the ZIP is opened again.
Check the return value for success and handle errors.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_comment
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the archive’s global comment, if any.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle (typically opened).
comment must not be NULL; on success it receives a pointer to an internal, null-terminated UTF-8 string or possibly NULL if no comment (not specified).
Do not modify or free the returned pointer; its lifetime is managed by the library.
Check return value before using the output.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_comment
functions.description: Sets the archive’s global comment to be written to the ZIP file when saving.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened in a mode that permits writing.
comment should be a null-terminated UTF-8 string; NULL handling is unspecified in this header.
Must be called before mz_zip_close to take effect.
Check return value to ensure the comment was accepted.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_version_madeby
functions.description: Retrieves the 'version made by' field value that identifies the originating platform/ZIP spec revision for central directory records.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
version_madeby must not be NULL.
Check return value for success before using the output.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_version_madeby
functions.description: Sets the 'version made by' field to be used when writing central directory entries.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle, opened in a mode that permits writing.
version_madeby must be a valid ZIP 'version made by' code; exact valid values are not documented here.
Call before writing entries or closing the archive for it to take effect.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_recover
functions.description: Enables or disables recovery mode that attempts to rebuild the central directory by scanning local file headers.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
recover is a boolean-like flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable).
Set this before operations that read the central directory.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_data_descriptor
functions.description: Enables or disables use of the ZIP data descriptor flag when writing entries.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened for writing.
data_descriptor is a boolean-like flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable).
Set before writing entries for consistent behavior.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_stream
functions.description: Retrieves the underlying stream pointer associated with the opened ZIP handle.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
stream must not be NULL; receives the stream pointer on success.
Do not assume ownership of the returned stream; lifetime is managed by the ZIP handle.
Check return value before using the output.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_cd_stream
functions.description: Specifies an alternate stream and starting position to read the central directory from (useful for multi-stream or in-memory central directory scenarios).
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
cd_stream must be a valid stream compatible with the library.
cd_start_pos should be a non-negative byte offset within cd_stream.
Call before reading the central directory (e.g., before locate/list operations).
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_cd_mem_stream
functions.description: Retrieves the memory-backed stream used to store the central directory, if applicable.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
cd_mem_stream must not be NULL; receives a pointer to the memory stream on success.
Do not free the returned stream; managed by the library.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_number_entry
functions.description: Sets the total number of entries for the archive (used when writing or managing multi-disk archives).
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle, typically in a state preparing for write/close.
number_entry must be the intended total count (must be >= 0; upper bounds not specified).
Call before writing the central directory if required by your workflow.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_number_entry
functions.description: Retrieves the total number of entries in the archive.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle (typically opened).
number_entry must not be NULL.
Check return value before using the output.

functions.name: mz_zip_set_disk_number_with_cd
functions.description: Sets the disk number that contains the central directory record (for multi-disk ZIPs).
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
disk_number_with_cd specifies the target disk index; valid range not documented here.
Set prior to operations that depend on central directory location.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_disk_number_with_cd
functions.description: Retrieves the disk number containing the central directory record.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
disk_number_with_cd must not be NULL.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_is_open
functions.description: Returns a non-zero value if a ZIP entry is currently open for read or write on this handle; zero otherwise.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle.
Use to guard read/write calls on entries.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_read_open
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_read_open(void *handle, uint8_t raw, const char *password);
functions.description: Opens the current entry for reading its data. Supports raw (compressed) or normal (decompressed) reads and optional decryption via password.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive.
A current entry must be selected (e.g., via mz_zip_goto_first_entry/mz_zip_goto_next_entry/mz_zip_locate_entry).
raw indicates raw read (compressed bytes) when non-zero; normal decompressed read when zero.
Provide password when the entry is encrypted; may be NULL for unencrypted entries (behavior for NULL on encrypted entries depends on library).
Must be closed with mz_zip_entry_read_close before opening another entry or closing the archive.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_read
functions.description: Reads up to len bytes from the currently open entry into buf. For normal reads, data is decompressed; for raw reads, compressed data is returned.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry opened by mz_zip_entry_read_open.
buf must not be NULL.
len must be >= 0 and indicates the size of buf in bytes.
Use the return value to determine the number of bytes read or end-of-stream; specific sentinel values are library-defined (not documented here).

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_read_close
functions.description: Closes the current entry after reading and optionally returns the data descriptor values: CRC-32, compressed size, and uncompressed size.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry opened for reading.
crc32, compressed_size, and uncompressed_size may be NULL if the values are not needed; if non-NULL they receive the corresponding values on success.
Must be called after mz_zip_entry_read_open/mz_zip_entry_read to finalize reading of the entry.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_write_open
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_write_open(void *handle, const mz_zip_file *file_info, int16_t compress_level, uint8_t raw, const char *password);
functions.description: Opens a new entry for writing data to the archive using the provided file metadata. Supports setting compression level, raw mode, and optional encryption via password.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened in a mode that permits writing.
file_info must not be NULL and should describe the entry (e.g., filename, attributes); required fields are not fully documented here.
compress_level must be a valid library-defined compression level; exact range not specified here.
raw non-zero indicates the caller will provide raw compressed data and will need to supply CRC/size at close.
password may be NULL for unencrypted entries; provide a non-NULL password for encryption as supported by the library.
Must be followed by one or more calls to mz_zip_entry_write and a closing call (mz_zip_entry_write_close or mz_zip_entry_close_raw/mz_zip_entry_close).
Check return value for success before writing.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_write
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_write(void *handle, const void *buf, int32_t len);
functions.description: Writes len bytes from buf to the currently open entry. Data may be compressed and/or encrypted according to the settings from write_open.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry opened for writing.
buf must not be NULL.
len must be >= 0 and must not exceed the available buffer size provided by the caller.
Check the return value to verify the number of bytes accepted or success/failure.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_write_close
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_write_close(void *handle, uint32_t crc32, int64_t compressed_size, int64_t uncompressed_size);
functions.description: Closes the current entry after writing and, when in raw mode, supplies the CRC-32 and sizes to be recorded in the data descriptor. In non-raw mode, these values may be ignored by the library.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry opened for writing.
If the entry was opened in raw mode, crc32, compressed_size, and uncompressed_size must match the data provided; otherwise behavior is undefined.
If not in raw mode, the parameters may be ignored; passing zeros is typically acceptable (not specified here).
Must be called exactly once per opened writable entry.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_seek_local_header
functions.description: Seeks the underlying stream to the local header of the current entry.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with a current entry selected.
Call only when the archive is opened and positioned on an entry.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_get_compress_stream
functions.description: Retrieves the compression stream used for the current entry (useful for advanced/custom IO scenarios).
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with a current entry (typically open for writing).
compress_stream must not be NULL; receives the stream pointer on success.
Do not free the returned stream; managed by the library.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_close_raw
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_close_raw(void *handle, int64_t uncompressed_size, uint32_t crc32);
functions.description: Closes the current entry when writing raw compressed data, providing the uncompressed size and CRC-32 to finalize metadata.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry opened for writing in raw mode.
uncompressed_size must match the actual uncompressed size of the data for the entry.
crc32 must be the CRC-32 of the uncompressed data.
Call exactly once per opened entry in this mode.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_close
functions.description: Closes the current entry (read or write) using default handling for metadata and descriptors.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry currently open.
Use this for non-raw cases or when explicit CRC/sizes are not required by the caller.
Call exactly once per opened entry.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_is_dir
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current entry represents a directory.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with a current entry selected (open or selected).

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_is_symlink
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current entry represents a symbolic link.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with a current entry selected (open or selected).

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_get_info
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the mz_zip_file metadata for the current entry. Valid only while the current entry is open.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry currently open.
file_info must not be NULL; receives a pointer to internal metadata on success.
The returned pointer is only valid while the entry remains open; do not free or modify it.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_get_local_info
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the local header metadata for the current entry. Valid only while the current entry is being read.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with an entry currently being read (opened for reading).
local_file_info must not be NULL; receives a pointer to internal metadata on success.
The returned pointer is only valid while reading remains active; do not free or modify it.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_entry_set_extrafield
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_entry_set_extrafield(void *handle, const uint8_t *extrafield, uint16_t extrafield_size);
functions.description: Sets or updates the extra field data for the current entry prior to writing the central directory.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle, with a current entry context for which the extra field is to be set.
extrafield may be NULL if clearing is supported; behavior not specified here.
extrafield_size must match the length of the extrafield buffer provided.
Call before the central directory is written (before closing the archive).
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_get_entry
functions.description: Returns the central directory offset (position) for the current entry within the ZIP file.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle with a current entry selected.
Use the return value directly; negative values may indicate errors depending on library conventions (not documented here).

functions.name: mz_zip_goto_entry
functions.description: Positions the current entry to the one located at the specified central directory position.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive.
cd_pos must be a valid central directory entry offset obtained from the library (e.g., via mz_zip_get_entry).
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_goto_first_entry
functions.description: Moves to the first entry in the archive for enumeration.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive.
Check return value; MZ_END_OF_LIST may indicate no entries (exact code not documented here).

functions.name: mz_zip_goto_next_entry
functions.description: Advances to the next entry in the archive or returns an end-of-list status when reaching the end.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive and positioned on an entry.
Check return value; a specific MZ_END_OF_LIST code is returned on completion (exact value not documented here).

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_entry
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_locate_entry(void *handle, const char *filename, uint8_t ignore_case);
functions.description: Searches for an entry by name and positions the current entry to it if found.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive.
filename must not be NULL and should be a null-terminated string.
ignore_case is a boolean-like flag controlling case sensitivity.
Check return value; a not-found status (e.g., MZ_END_OF_LIST) is returned if not located (exact code not documented here).

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_first_entry
functions.description: Locates the first entry that matches the user-supplied callback predicate, positioning the current entry to that item.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive.
cb must not be NULL and must conform to mz_zip_locate_entry_cb signature.
userdata is passed through to the callback; may be NULL.
Check return value to distinguish success from not-found.

functions.name: mz_zip_locate_next_entry
functions.description: Continues locating the next entry that matches the user-supplied callback predicate, starting after the current match.
requirements: handle must be a valid ZIP handle opened on an archive and positioned by a prior locate operation.
cb must not be NULL and must conform to mz_zip_locate_entry_cb signature.
userdata is passed through to the callback; may be NULL.
Check return value to distinguish success from not-found.

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_is_dir
functions.description: Determines whether the given attribute flags represent a directory on the specified originating platform.
requirements: attrib must contain file attribute bits from the ZIP entry.
version_madeby must indicate the originating host system; valid values not documented here.

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_is_symlink
functions.description: Determines whether the given attribute flags represent a symbolic link on the specified originating platform.
requirements: attrib must contain file attribute bits from the ZIP entry.
version_madeby must indicate the originating host system; valid values not documented here.

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_convert
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_attrib_convert(uint8_t src_sys, uint32_t src_attrib, uint8_t target_sys, uint32_t *target_attrib);
functions.description: Converts file attribute bits from one host system representation to another.
requirements: src_sys and target_sys must be valid host system identifiers as used by ZIP (values not documented here).
target_attrib must not be NULL; receives the converted attribute bits.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_posix_to_win32
functions.description: Converts POSIX file attributes to Win32 file attributes.
requirements: win32_attrib must not be NULL.
posix_attrib must contain valid POSIX attribute bits expected by the library.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_attrib_win32_to_posix
functions.description: Converts Win32 file attributes to POSIX file attributes.
requirements: posix_attrib must not be NULL.
win32_attrib must contain valid Win32 attribute bits expected by the library.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_find
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_find(void *stream, uint16_t type, int32_t max_seek, uint16_t *length);
functions.description: Seeks within a stream to locate an extra field with the specified type and returns its length.
requirements: stream must be a valid readable/seekable stream compatible with the library.
type specifies the extra field header ID to find.
max_seek should be >= 0 and limits how far the function will search within the stream.
length must not be NULL; receives the extra field data length on success.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_contains
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_contains(const uint8_t *extrafield, int32_t extrafield_size, uint16_t type, uint16_t *length);
functions.description: Checks whether an in-memory extrafield blob contains an entry of the given type and, if so, returns its size.
requirements: extrafield may be NULL only if extrafield_size is 0; otherwise it must point to a buffer of at least extrafield_size bytes.
extrafield_size must be >= 0.
type specifies the extra field header ID to look for.
length must not be NULL; receives the size of the matching extrafield on success.
Check return value for success or not-found.

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_read
functions.description: Reads an extrafield header (type and length) from the given stream at the current position.
requirements: stream must be a valid readable stream compatible with the library.
type must not be NULL; receives the extrafield header ID.
length must not be NULL; receives the extrafield data length.
Stream must be positioned at an extrafield header before calling.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_extrafield_write
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_extrafield_write(void *stream, uint16_t type, uint16_t length);
functions.description: Writes an extrafield header (type and length) to the given stream at the current position.
requirements: stream must be a valid writable stream compatible with the library.
type specifies the extrafield header ID to write.
length specifies the extrafield data length that will follow the header if written by the caller.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_dosdate_to_tm
functions.description: Converts a DOS date/time value to a struct tm.
requirements: ptm must not be NULL; receives the converted time components.
dos_date must be a valid DOS date/time value.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_dosdate_to_time_t
functions.description: Converts a DOS date/time value to a time_t (Unix epoch seconds).
requirements: dos_date must be a valid DOS date/time value.
Use the returned time_t directly; error signaling is not documented here.

functions.name: mz_zip_tm_to_time_t
functions.description: Converts a struct tm to a time_t (Unix epoch seconds).
requirements: ptm must not be NULL and must contain a valid broken-down time.
The function may rely on the platform’s mktime-like behavior; error handling not documented here.

functions.name: mz_zip_time_t_to_tm
functions.description: Converts a time_t (Unix epoch seconds) to a struct tm.
requirements: ptm must not be NULL; receives the converted broken-down time.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_time_t_to_dos_date
functions.description: Converts a time_t to a DOS date/time value.
requirements: unix_time must be a valid time_t.
Returned value is a packed DOS date/time; error signaling is not documented.

functions.name: mz_zip_tm_to_dosdate
functions.description: Converts a struct tm to a DOS date/time value.
requirements: ptm must not be NULL and must contain a valid broken-down time.
Returned value is a packed DOS date/time; error signaling is not documented.

functions.name: mz_zip_ntfs_to_unix_time
functions.description: Converts an NTFS file time (100-ns intervals since Windows epoch) to Unix time_t seconds.
requirements: unix_time must not be NULL; receives the converted time.
ntfs_time must be a valid NTFS timestamp.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_unix_to_ntfs_time
functions.description: Converts Unix time_t seconds to an NTFS file time (100-ns intervals since Windows epoch).
requirements: ntfs_time must not be NULL; receives the converted time.
unix_time must be a valid time_t value.
Check return value for success.

functions.name: mz_zip_path_compare
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_path_compare(const char *path1, const char *path2, uint8_t ignore_case);
functions.description: Compares two paths, ignoring differences in slash direction and optionally case, returning a comparison result.
requirements: path1 and path2 must not be NULL and should be null-terminated strings.
ignore_case is a boolean-like flag controlling case-insensitive comparison.
Interpretation of the return value follows library conventions (negative/zero/positive not documented).

functions.name: mz_zip_get_compression_method_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given compression method identifier.
requirements: compression_method must be a valid method code as used by the library.
The returned pointer is to a static or internal string; do not modify or free it.
If the method is unknown, the returned string content is library-defined.

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_is_open
functions.description: Checks whether a zip reader instance currently has an archive open. Use to verify state before performing operations that require an open archive.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create
Function may be called at any time to query open state

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading from an abstract stream. Use this when you have a custom stream implementation.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create and not already open
stream must point to a valid readable stream compatible with the library’s expected stream interface (exact type unknown)
Must close with mz_zip_reader_close when finished

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_file
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading from a file path.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create and not already open
path must be a valid, null-terminated file system path to an existing zip file
Must close with mz_zip_reader_close when finished

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_file_in_memory
functions.description: Opens a zip archive by loading the file at the given path into memory for faster access, then reading from that memory image.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create and not already open
path must be a valid, null-terminated file system path to an existing zip file
Must close with mz_zip_reader_close when finished

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_open_buffer
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_reader_open_buffer(void *handle, const uint8_t *buf, int32_t len, uint8_t copy);
functions.description: Opens a zip archive for reading from a memory buffer.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create and not already open
buf must point to a buffer containing the entire zip file image
len must be non-negative and specify the size of buf in bytes
copy selects whether the implementation copies the buffer (exact behavior beyond this flag is unknown)
Must close with mz_zip_reader_close when finished

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_close
functions.description: Closes the currently open zip archive for the reader and releases any associated resources.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance created by mz_zip_reader_create
Archive should have been opened successfully before calling close
After closing, the handle can be reused to open another archive or deleted via mz_zip_reader_delete

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_unzip_cd
functions.description: Unzips (extracts/loads) the central directory of the opened archive, preparing entry metadata for fast access.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
Should be called after a successful open and before operations that rely on central directory details (if needed)

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_goto_first_entry
functions.description: Positions the reader at the first entry that matches the current pattern filter, if any.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
Optional pattern must have been set previously via mz_zip_reader_set_pattern to filter entries; otherwise all entries are considered

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_goto_next_entry
functions.description: Advances to the next entry that matches the current pattern filter.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
Call after mz_zip_reader_goto_first_entry or a previous successful mz_zip_reader_goto_next_entry

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_locate_entry
functions.signature: int32_t mz_zip_reader_locate_entry(void *handle, const char *filename, uint8_t ignore_case);
functions.description: Locates an entry by filename within the open archive, with optional case-insensitive matching.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
filename must be a valid, null-terminated string naming the entry to locate

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_open
functions.description: Opens the current located entry for reading its data.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
There must be a current entry selected (via locate or goto functions) before calling
Must be paired with mz_zip_reader_entry_close after finishing read/save operations on the entry

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_close
functions.description: Closes the currently open entry and finalizes any entry-level operations.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
An entry must have been opened by mz_zip_reader_entry_open

functions.name: mz_zip_reader_entry_read
functions.description: Reads data from the currently opened entry into the provided buffer.
requirements: handle must be a valid zip reader instance with an archive open
An entry must be opened via mz_zip_reader_entry_open before reading
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes

functions.description: Configures the AES context for decryption with the provided key and initialization vector (IV).
requirements: handle must be a valid AES context created by mz_crypt_aes_create().
key must point to at least key_length bytes; key_length must be appropriate for the selected AES mode/algorithm (exact valid lengths are not specified here).
iv must point to at least iv_length bytes; iv_length must match the requirements of the selected AES mode (exact valid lengths are not specified here).
Must be called before mz_crypt_aes_decrypt()/mz_crypt_aes_decrypt_final().
Returns an int32_t status code; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_aes_set_mode
functions.description: Sets the AES cipher mode to be used (e.g., CBC/CTR/GCM). Specific mode constants are not defined in this header.
requirements: handle must be a valid AES context created by mz_crypt_aes_create().
mode must be a valid mode identifier recognized by the implementation; exact values are unknown from this header.
Should be called before setting keys and performing encryption/decryption so that parameter sizes (e.g., IV length, tag usage) are consistent.

functions.name: mz_crypt_aes_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new AES cipher context handle to be used with the AES functions.
requirements: Caller must check the returned handle for NULL to detect allocation or initialization failure.
The returned handle must be freed with mz_crypt_aes_delete().

functions.name: mz_crypt_aes_delete
functions.description: Destroys and frees an AES cipher context created by mz_crypt_aes_create(), and sets the caller’s handle pointer to NULL.
requirements: handle must be a non-NULL pointer to a handle variable previously returned by mz_crypt_aes_create().
*handle must be either NULL or a valid AES context; passing an invalid pointer results in undefined behavior.
After return, *handle is set to NULL (implementation-dependent but expected from typical patterns).

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_reset
functions.description: Resets the HMAC context state so a new MAC computation can start without recreating the handle.
requirements: handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create().

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_init
functions.signature: int32_t mz_crypt_hmac_init(void *handle, const void *key, int32_t key_length);
functions.description: Initializes the HMAC context with the provided key for a new MAC computation.
requirements: handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create().
key must point to at least key_length bytes when key_length > 0; key may be NULL only if key_length == 0.
key_length must be >= 0 (exact acceptable sizes depend on the selected algorithm and are not specified here).
Returns an int32_t status code; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_update
functions.signature: int32_t mz_crypt_hmac_update(void *handle, const void *buf, int32_t size);
functions.description: Feeds message data into the ongoing HMAC computation.
requirements: handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create() and initialized via mz_crypt_hmac_init().
buf must point to at least size bytes when size > 0; buf may be NULL only if size == 0.
size must be >= 0.
Returns an int32_t status code; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_end
functions.description: Finalizes the HMAC computation and writes the MAC to the provided buffer.
requirements: handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create() and initialized via mz_crypt_hmac_init().
digest must point to a writable buffer of at least digest_size bytes.
digest_size must be large enough for the selected HMAC algorithm’s output; exact size is not specified here.
Returns an int32_t status code; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_copy
functions.description: Copies the internal state of one HMAC context to another, allowing duplication or branching of the computation.
requirements: src_handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create().
target_handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create().
Both contexts should be compatible (same algorithm and key) for a meaningful copy; specifics are not defined here.
Returns an int32_t status code; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_set_algorithm
functions.description: Selects the hash algorithm used by the HMAC context (e.g., HMAC-SHA1/HMAC-SHA256). Specific algorithm identifiers are not defined in this header.
requirements: handle must be a valid HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create().
Should be called before mz_crypt_hmac_init() to affect the next computation.
algorithm must be a valid identifier recognized by the implementation; exact values are unknown from this header.

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_create
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new HMAC context handle to be used with the HMAC functions.
requirements: Caller must check the returned handle for NULL to detect allocation or initialization failure.
The returned handle must be freed with mz_crypt_hmac_delete().

functions.name: mz_crypt_hmac_delete
functions.description: Destroys and frees a HMAC context created by mz_crypt_hmac_create(), and sets the caller’s handle pointer to NULL.
requirements: handle must be a non-NULL pointer to a handle variable previously returned by mz_crypt_hmac_create().
*handle must be either NULL or a valid HMAC context; passing an invalid pointer results in undefined behavior.
After return, *handle is set to NULL (implementation-dependent but expected from typical patterns).

functions.name: unzOpen
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive by filesystem path and returns an unzip handle (unzFile) to iterate entries and read file data.
requirements: path must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated string naming a ZIP file location accessible to the I/O layer
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose when no longer needed
Do not use the handle after unzClose returns

functions.name: unzOpen64
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive using a 64-bit compatible path parameter type for broader ABI compatibility; returns an unzip handle.
requirements: path must be a non-null pointer; expected to reference a NUL-terminated path string
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose
Do not use the handle after unzClose

functions.name: unzOpen2
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive by path using a custom 32-bit zlib I/O function table (zlib_filefunc_def).
requirements: path must be a non-null NUL-terminated string
pzlib_filefunc_def may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL it must point to a fully initialized I/O function table compatible with zlib_filefunc_def
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose
Do not use the handle after unzClose

functions.name: unzOpen2_64
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive using a custom 64-bit zlib I/O function table (zlib_filefunc64_def).
requirements: path must be a non-null pointer to the path (typically a NUL-terminated string)
pzlib_filefunc_def may be NULL to use defaults; if non-NULL it must point to a fully initialized zlib_filefunc64_def
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose
Do not use the handle after unzClose

functions.name: unzClose
functions.description: Closes an opened unzip handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: file must be a valid unzFile previously returned by an unzOpen* function
Must not be called more than once on the same handle
After closing, no further API calls using this handle are allowed

functions.name: unzGetGlobalInfo
functions.description: Retrieves global information from the opened ZIP (central directory) into a 32-bit compatible structure.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
pglobal_info32 must be a non-null pointer to writable memory

functions.name: unzGetGlobalInfo64
functions.description: Retrieves global information from the opened ZIP into a 64-bit structure (supports large archives).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
pglobal_info must be a non-null pointer to writable memory

functions.name: unzGetGlobalComment
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzGetGlobalComment(unzFile file, char *comment, unsigned long comment_size);
functions.description: Copies the ZIP file global comment into the caller buffer up to comment_size bytes.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
If comment_size > 0, comment must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of at least comment_size bytes
comment may be NULL only if comment_size is 0

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile
functions.description: Opens the current ZIP entry for reading (decompressing) using default settings.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry (via unzGoToFirstFile/unzGoToNextFile/unzLocateFile/etc.)
Each successful open must be matched by unzCloseCurrentFile before moving to another entry or closing the archive

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFilePassword
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzOpenCurrentFilePassword(unzFile file, const char *password);
functions.description: Opens the current ZIP entry for reading with a password for encrypted entries.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
password must be a NUL-terminated string; may be required for encrypted entries
Must call unzCloseCurrentFile after use

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile2
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzOpenCurrentFile2(unzFile file, int *method, int *level, int raw);
functions.description: Opens the current ZIP entry for reading and optionally returns the compression method and level; can request raw (no decompression) access.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
If method is non-NULL it must point to writable int storage
If level is non-NULL it must point to writable int storage
raw must be 0 or non-zero to indicate decompression vs raw mode (exact semantics not documented here)
Must call unzCloseCurrentFile after use

functions.name: unzOpenCurrentFile3
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzOpenCurrentFile3(unzFile file, int *method, int *level, int raw, const char *password);
functions.description: Opens the current ZIP entry for reading with optional method/level output, optional raw mode, and an optional password for encrypted entries.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
If method is non-NULL it must point to writable int storage
If level is non-NULL it must point to writable int storage
raw must be 0 or non-zero to indicate decompression vs raw mode
password may be NULL for non-encrypted entries; if provided must be NUL-terminated
Must call unzCloseCurrentFile after use

functions.name: unzReadCurrentFile
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzReadCurrentFile(unzFile file, void *buf, uint32_t len);
functions.description: Reads (decompresses) up to len bytes from the currently opened ZIP entry into buf; returns number of bytes read or a negative error code.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with a current entry opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*
buf must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least len bytes when len > 0
len may be 0 (no data read)
Callers should loop until 0 indicates EOF or a negative value indicates error; ensure unzCloseCurrentFile is called afterward

functions.name: unzCloseCurrentFile
functions.description: Closes the currently opened ZIP entry, finalizing any pending CRC checks and releasing per-entry resources.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry previously opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*
Must be called exactly once for each successful unzOpenCurrentFile* call before moving to another entry or closing the archive

functions.name: unzGetCurrentFileInfo
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzGetCurrentFileInfo(unzFile file, unz_file_info *pfile_info, char *filename, unsigned long filename_size, void *extrafield, unsigned long extrafield_size, char *comment, unsigned long comment_size);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for the current ZIP entry into provided structures/buffers (32-bit sizes).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
pfile_info may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable unz_file_info storage
If filename_size > 0, filename must be a non-null buffer of at least filename_size bytes
If extrafield_size > 0, extrafield must be a non-null buffer of at least extrafield_size bytes
If comment_size > 0, comment must be a non-null buffer of at least comment_size bytes

functions.name: unzGetCurrentFileInfo64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzGetCurrentFileInfo64(unzFile file, unz_file_info64 *pfile_info, char *filename, unsigned long filename_size, void *extrafield, unsigned long extrafield_size, char *comment, unsigned long comment_size);
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for the current ZIP entry into provided structures/buffers (64-bit sizes).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
pfile_info may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable unz_file_info64 storage
If filename_size > 0, filename must be a non-null buffer of at least filename_size bytes
If extrafield_size > 0, extrafield must be a non-null buffer of at least extrafield_size bytes
If comment_size > 0, comment must be a non-null buffer of at least comment_size bytes

functions.name: unzGoToFirstFile
functions.description: Positions the iterator to the first file entry in the ZIP archive.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
Any previously opened current file must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before repositioning

functions.name: unzGoToNextFile
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next file entry in the ZIP archive.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry
Any currently opened entry must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before advancing

functions.name: unzLocateFile
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzLocateFile(unzFile file, const char *filename, unzFileNameCase filename_case);
functions.description: Locates an entry by name and positions the iterator to it; name comparison behavior is specified by filename_case (legacy signature).
requirements: This overload is available when MZ_COMPAT_VERSION is undefined or < 110 at compile time
file must be a valid, open unzFile
filename must be a non-null NUL-terminated string
filename_case controls case sensitivity per documented values (0 OS default, 1 case sensitive, >=2 ignore case)

functions.name: unzGetLocalExtrafield
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzGetLocalExtrafield(unzFile file, void *buf, unsigned int len);
functions.description: Reads the local header extra field of the current entry into buf up to len bytes.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry; typically requires the entry to be opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*
If len > 0, buf must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least len bytes

functions.name: unzOpen_MZ
functions.description: Compatibility helper that opens an unzip handle from an existing minizip-ng stream object.
requirements: stream must be a valid pointer to a minizip-ng stream compatible with this API (exact type not specified in this header)
The returned unzFile must be closed with unzClose_MZ or unzClose per intended usage

functions.name: unzClose_MZ
functions.description: Closes an unzip handle previously created by unzOpen_MZ, with compatibility to older minizip-ng behavior.
requirements: file must be a valid unzFile returned by unzOpen_MZ
Must not be called more than once on the same handle
After closing, no further API calls using this handle are allowed

functions.name: unzGetHandle_MZ
functions.description: Returns the underlying minizip-ng handle associated with the given unzFile (compatibility accessor).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile

functions.name: unzGetStream_MZ
functions.description: Returns the underlying stream object associated with the given unzFile (compatibility accessor).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile

functions.name: unzGetFilePos
functions.description: Retrieves the current entry position information in 32-bit compatible form.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
file_pos must be a non-null pointer to writable unz_file_pos storage

functions.name: unzGoToFilePos
functions.description: Seeks to the entry designated by a previously captured unz_file_pos (32-bit).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
file_pos must be a non-null pointer to a position previously obtained from the same or an equivalent archive
Any currently opened entry must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before repositioning

functions.name: unzGetFilePos64
functions.description: Retrieves the current entry position information in 64-bit form.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
file_pos must be a non-null pointer to writable unz64_file_pos storage

functions.name: unzGoToFilePos64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzGoToFilePos64(unzFile file, const unz64_file_pos *file_pos);
functions.description: Seeks to the entry designated by a previously captured unz64_file_pos.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
file_pos must be a non-null pointer to a position previously obtained from the same or an equivalent archive
Any currently opened entry must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before repositioning

functions.name: unzGetOffset64
functions.description: Returns the 64-bit byte offset of the current entry within the ZIP central directory or archive (implementation-dependent).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry

functions.name: unzGetOffset
functions.description: Returns the 32-bit byte offset of the current entry (legacy API).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile positioned on a file entry

functions.name: unzSetOffset64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzSetOffset64(unzFile file, int64_t pos);
functions.description: Sets the 64-bit byte offset used to locate the current entry (low-level positioning).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
pos should be a valid offset within the archive (exact semantics unspecified in this header)
Any currently opened entry must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before repositioning

functions.name: unzSetOffset
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzSetOffset(unzFile file, unsigned long pos);
functions.description: Sets the 32-bit byte offset used to locate the current entry (legacy API).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile
pos should be a valid 32-bit offset within the archive
Any currently opened entry must be closed via unzCloseCurrentFile before repositioning

functions.name: unztell
functions.description: Returns the current read position (offset) within the currently opened entry as a 32-bit value (compatibility).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unztell64
functions.description: Returns the current read position within the currently opened entry as a 64-bit value.
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unzeof
functions.description: Indicates end-of-file state for the currently opened entry (non-zero at EOF, zero otherwise).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unzTell
functions.description: Compatibility alias of unztell: returns the current read position within the opened entry (32-bit).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unzTell64
functions.description: Compatibility alias of unztell64: returns the current read position within the opened entry (64-bit).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unzSeek
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzSeek(unzFile file, int32_t offset, int origin);
functions.description: Seeks within the currently opened entry to a position determined by offset and origin (compatibility API).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*
origin should be a valid seek origin constant (e.g., SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END) appropriate to this API

functions.name: unzSeek64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int unzSeek64(unzFile file, int64_t offset, int origin);
functions.description: Seeks within the currently opened entry using a 64-bit offset and origin (compatibility API).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*
origin should be a valid seek origin constant appropriate to this API

functions.name: unzEndOfFile
functions.description: Compatibility API that reports if the currently opened entry is at end-of-file (non-zero at EOF).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile with an entry currently opened via unzOpenCurrentFile*

functions.name: unzGetStream
functions.description: Returns the underlying stream associated with the given unzFile (modern compatibility accessor).
requirements: file must be a valid, open unzFile

functions.name: zipOpen
functions.signature: ZEXPORT zipFile zipOpen(const char *path, int append);
functions.description: Opens (or creates/appends to) a ZIP archive by filesystem path using the default I/O layer. Returns an opaque zipFile handle on success, or NULL on failure. Use this handle to add files, then close with zipClose.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated filesystem path string.
append must be one of APPEND_STATUS_CREATE, APPEND_STATUS_CREATEAFTER, or APPEND_STATUS_ADDINZIP.
Caller must close the returned handle with zipClose (or compatible close) when finished.
On failure, the function returns NULL and no handle must be used.

functions.name: zipOpen64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT zipFile zipOpen64(const void *path, int append);
functions.description: Opens (or creates/appends to) a ZIP archive using a path passed as a generic pointer (commonly to support platform-specific path types such as wide strings). Returns a zipFile handle on success, or NULL on failure.
requirements: path must reference a valid path object appropriate for the build/platform. Exact type is platform-specific and not specified in this header.
append must be one of APPEND_STATUS_CREATE, APPEND_STATUS_CREATEAFTER, or APPEND_STATUS_ADDINZIP.
Caller must close the returned handle with zipClose (or compatible close) when finished.
On failure, the function returns NULL and no handle must be used.

functions.name: zipOpen2
functions.signature: ZEXPORT zipFile zipOpen2(const char *path, int append, zipcharpc *globalcomment, zlib_filefunc_def *pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive by path with control over the I/O callbacks (zlib_filefunc_def). Returns a zipFile handle on success. Provides compatibility with the original minizip API.
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated filesystem path string.
append must be one of APPEND_STATUS_CREATE, APPEND_STATUS_CREATEAFTER, or APPEND_STATUS_ADDINZIP.
pzlib_filefunc_def must point to a properly initialized zlib_filefunc_def describing the desired I/O API; may be NULL to use defaults (inferred from typical minizip patterns).
globalcomment is an output parameter pointer location for the global ZIP comment or may be NULL if not needed (inferred from name/pattern); exact semantics are not documented here.
Caller must close the returned handle with zipClose (or compatible close) when finished.
On failure, the function returns NULL and no handle must be used.

functions.name: zipOpen2_64
functions.signature: ZEXPORT zipFile zipOpen2_64(const void *path, int append, zipcharpc *globalcomment, zlib_filefunc64_def *pzlib_filefunc_def);
functions.description: Opens a ZIP archive with a generic-path pointer and a 64-bit capable I/O callback table. Returns a zipFile handle on success. Use for large files or custom I/O.
requirements: path must reference a valid path object appropriate for the build/platform.
append must be one of APPEND_STATUS_CREATE, APPEND_STATUS_CREATEAFTER, or APPEND_STATUS_ADDINZIP.
pzlib_filefunc64_def must point to a properly initialized zlib_filefunc64_def; may be NULL to use defaults (inferred from minizip patterns).
globalcomment is an output parameter pointer location for the global ZIP comment or may be NULL if not needed (inferred).
Caller must close the returned handle with zipClose (or compatible close) when finished.
On failure, the function returns NULL and no handle must be used.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip
functions.description: Starts a new file entry inside an open ZIP archive and prepares to write its data using default compression settings. After a successful call, write data with zipWriteInFileInZip and finish with zipCloseFileInZip (or Raw variants if using raw mode in other overloads).
requirements: file must be a valid zipFile obtained from zipOpen/zipOpen2/zipOpen64/etc. and not yet closed.
filename must be a valid, null-terminated path within the ZIP; must not be NULL.
zipfi may be NULL or point to metadata (timestamps/attributes).
If size_extrafield_local > 0, extrafield_local must be non-NULL; if extrafield_local is NULL, size_extrafield_local must be 0.
If size_extrafield_global > 0, extrafield_global must be non-NULL; if extrafield_global is NULL, size_extrafield_global must be 0.
comment may be NULL or a null-terminated string.
compression_method and level must be acceptable by the underlying zlib/deflate implementation; exact valid values are not specified here.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values (e.g., ZIP_PARAMERROR, ZIP_INTERNALERROR) indicate failure and the file entry is not open.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip64
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with optional Zip64 support. Use when file sizes may exceed 4GB or when forcing Zip64 structures. Write file data with zipWriteInFileInZip and close with zipCloseFileInZip/zipCloseFileInZip64 as appropriate.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip apply.
zip64 indicates whether to use Zip64 for the entry; nonzero typically enables Zip64 (inferred from naming).
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip2
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with a flag to write raw (pre-compressed) data. If raw is set, the caller must later close using a Raw close (providing size/CRC) or use the matching close function that accepts raw parameters.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip apply.

raw controls whether the data is written raw (no compression/headers managed by library); if raw != 0, caller is responsible for providing CRC and uncompressed size at close via zipCloseFileInZipRaw/zipCloseFileInZipRaw64.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip2_64
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with raw mode and optional Zip64 support. Intended for large files and/or when the caller manages CRC/size explicitly.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip2 apply.
zip64 indicates whether to use Zip64 structures for the entry.
If raw is enabled, caller must provide correct CRC and sizes to the Raw close function.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip3
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with extended zlib compression parameters and optional traditional ZIP encryption. After opening, write data with zipWriteInFileInZip and close with the appropriate close function.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip2 apply.
windowBits, memLevel, and strategy must be valid values for zlib's deflateInit2; invalid values may cause failure.
If password is non-NULL, traditional ZIP encryption is enabled; crc_for_crypting must be the CRC-32 of the uncompressed data (standard minizip behavior).
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip3_64
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with extended zlib parameters, optional encryption, and explicit Zip64 control.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip3 apply.
zip64 indicates whether to use Zip64 structures for the entry.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip4
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with extended compression parameters, optional encryption, and explicit control of ZIP header fields (version_madeby and base flags).
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip3 apply.
version_madeby must be a valid ZIP "version made by" field value per the ZIP specification; exact composition is not documented here.
flag_base provides base general-purpose bit flags to set; must be a valid combination per ZIP spec.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipOpenNewFileInZip4_64
functions.description: Starts a new file entry with full control over compression, encryption, header fields, and Zip64 usage.
requirements: All requirements from zipOpenNewFileInZip4 apply.
zip64 indicates whether to use Zip64 structures for the entry.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipWriteInFileInZip
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int zipWriteInFileInZip(zipFile file, const void *buf, uint32_t len);
functions.description: Writes raw data bytes to the currently open file entry within the ZIP. May be called repeatedly until all data is written, then the entry must be closed.
requirements: file must be a valid zipFile with an open file entry previously started by zipOpenNewFileInZip* and not yet closed.
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; must not be NULL when len > 0.
len is the number of bytes to write; may be 0 to perform a no-op write.
Returns ZIP_OK (0) on success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: zipCloseFileInZipRaw
functions.signature: ZEXPORT int zipCloseFileInZipRaw(zipFile file, unsigned long uncompressed_size, unsigned long crc32);
functions.description: Closes the current file entry when it was opened in raw mode, providing the uncompressed size and CRC-32 explicitly so headers can be finalized.
requirements: file must be a valid zipFile with an open file entry that was created with raw mode enabled (via a zipOpenNewFileInZip* function supporting raw).
