import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Goal: produce a valid, interesting arbitrary binary file suitable for minizip-ng raw stream and OS APIs.
# The fuzzer provides this buffer as the content of a temporary file referenced by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME().
# We focus on producing contents that exercise:
# - Reading/writing/copying streams
# - Finding forward/reverse byte sequences (needles)
# - Seeking/telling (varied sizes, repetitive and unique regions)
# - File CRC queries and ZIP open attempts (optionally make some buffers valid ZIPs)
# - Symlink reads (path only, content irrelevant) -> still keep content valid
#
# Strategy:
# 1) With seeded RNG, choose from several corpus templates:
#    - Random bytes with embedded ASCII and binary patterns
#    - Highly compressible data (runs, small alphabet)
#    - Repeated blocks enabling find/find_reverse across boundaries
#    - ZIP file (PK\x03\x04 ... central directory ... end of central directory) minimal but valid
#    - Zeros or 0xFF padded with headers to test edge seeks
# 2) Insert multiple common needles and their reverse, at varying offsets.
# 3) Keep size <= 4096.
#
# The generator returns the bytes; framework will persist it to a file.

ASCII_NEEDLES = [
    b"needle",
    b"NEEDLE",
    b"Minizip",
    b"PKZIP",
    b"hello world",
    b"1234567890",
    b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04",
]

BINARY_NEEDLES = [
    b"\x50\x4b\x03\x04",  # local file header signature
    b"\x50\x4b\x01\x02",  # central directory signature
    b"\x50\x4b\x05\x06",  # EOCD signature
    b"\x1f\x8b\x08",       # gzip header
    b"\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd",  # zstd magic
]


def _rand(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_repeated_blocks(r: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    blocks: List[bytes] = []
    base_patterns = [
        b"A" * 32,
        b"B" * 64,
        (b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. ")[:64],
        _rand(r, 16),
    ]
    while sum(len(b) for b in blocks) < total:
        pat = r.choice(base_patterns)
        rep = r.randint(1, 8)
        blocks.append(pat * rep)
    data = b"".join(blocks)
    return data[:total]


def _insert_needles(r: random.Random, buf: bytearray) -> None:
    # Insert multiple distinct needles at random offsets within buffer
    needles = ASCII_NEEDLES + BINARY_NEEDLES
    r.shuffle(needles)
    for nd in needles[: r.randint(3, min(8, len(needles)))]:
        if len(buf) < len(nd) + 1:
            break
        pos = r.randint(0, max(0, len(buf) - len(nd)))
        buf[pos : pos + len(nd)] = nd


def _make_highly_compressible(r: random.Random, total: int) -> bytes:
    # 90% from small alphabet, long runs
    out = bytearray()
    alphabet = [b"\x00", b"\x20", b"A", b"B", b"C", b"\n"]
    while len(out) < total:
        ch = r.choice(alphabet)
        run = r.randint(1, 128)
        out += ch * run
    return bytes(out[:total])


def _make_zip_minimal(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal ZIP with a single file “file.txt” containing small data.
    # Structure: Local File Header + Filename + Data + Central Directory + EOCD
    # Signatures per ZIP spec.
    def u16(x):
        return struct.pack("<H", x)
    def u32(x):
        return struct.pack("<I", x)

    fname = b"file.txt"
    data_choices = [b"hello world\n", b"minizip-ng test\n", _rand(r, r.randint(1, 64))]
    file_data = r.choice(data_choices)

    # Compute CRC-32 using binascii
    import binascii

    crc32 = binascii.crc32(file_data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    comp_method = 0  # store
    gp_flag = 0
    ver = 20
    dos_time = 0
    dos_date = 0

    # Local file header
    lfh = []
    lfh.append(b"\x50\x4b\x03\x04")  # signature
    lfh.append(u16(ver))                 # version needed to extract
    lfh.append(u16(gp_flag))             # general purpose bit flag
    lfh.append(u16(comp_method))         # compression method
    lfh.append(u16(dos_time))            # file mod time
    lfh.append(u16(dos_date))            # file mod date
    lfh.append(u32(crc32))               # crc-32
    lfh.append(u32(len(file_data)))      # compressed size
    lfh.append(u32(len(file_data)))      # uncompressed size
    lfh.append(u16(len(fname)))          # file name length
    lfh.append(u16(0))                   # extra field length
    lfh_bytes = b"".join(lfh)

    local_offset = 0  # since we'll place LFH at start
    local_part = lfh_bytes + fname + file_data

    # Central directory header for the same entry
    cdh = []
    cdh.append(b"\x50\x4b\x01\x02")  # central file header signature
    cdh.append(u16(0x0314))             # version made by (arbitrary)
    cdh.append(u16(ver))                # version needed to extract
    cdh.append(u16(gp_flag))            # general purpose bit flag
    cdh.append(u16(comp_method))        # compression method
    cdh.append(u16(dos_time))
    cdh.append(u16(dos_date))
    cdh.append(u32(crc32))
    cdh.append(u32(len(file_data)))
    cdh.append(u32(len(file_data)))
    cdh.append(u16(len(fname)))         # file name length
    cdh.append(u16(0))                  # extra field length
    cdh.append(u16(0))                  # file comment length
    cdh.append(u16(0))                  # disk number start
    cdh.append(u16(0))                  # internal file attributes
    cdh.append(u32(0))                  # external file attributes
    cdh.append(u32(local_offset))       # relative offset of local header
    cdh_bytes = b"".join(cdh)
    cd_part = cdh_bytes + fname

    # End of central directory
    eocd = []
    eocd.append(b"\x50\x4b\x05\x06")  # EOCD signature
    eocd.append(u16(0))                   # number of this disk
    eocd.append(u16(0))                   # disk with start of CD
    eocd.append(u16(1))                   # total entries on this disk
    eocd.append(u16(1))                   # total entries
    eocd.append(u32(len(cd_part)))        # size of central directory
    eocd.append(u32(len(local_part)))     # offset of central directory
    eocd.append(u16(0))                   # zip file comment length
    eocd_bytes = b"".join(eocd)

    blob = local_part + cd_part + eocd_bytes
    return blob


def _mix_patterns(r: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a composite buffer: header zone, body zone, trailer zone
    zones: List[bytes] = []
    # Zone 1: random header with magic markers
    header_size = min(128, size // 8 + r.randint(0, 64))
    header = bytearray(_rand(r, max(0, header_size)))
    _insert_needles(r, header)
    zones.append(bytes(header))

    remaining = max(0, size - sum(len(z) for z in zones))
    if remaining <= 0:
        return b"".join(zones)[:size]

    # Zone 2: body: choose repeated or compressible pattern
    body_choice = r.randint(0, 2)
    body_len = max(0, int(remaining * 0.75))
    if body_choice == 0:
        body = _make_repeated_blocks(r, body_len)
    elif body_choice == 1:
        body = _make_highly_compressible(r, body_len)
    else:
        body = _rand(r, body_len)
    zones.append(body)

    remaining = max(0, size - sum(len(z) for z in zones))
    # Zone 3: trailer with signatures placed near end
    trailer = bytearray(_rand(r, remaining))
    _insert_needles(r, trailer)
    zones.append(bytes(trailer))

    combined = b"".join(zones)[:size]
    return combined


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Target total size up to 4096; prefer a range that exercises IO without being huge
    size_choices = [r.randint(64, 256), r.randint(256, 1024), r.randint(1024, 3072), r.randint(3072, 4096)]
    size = r.choice(size_choices)

    # Choose a template
    template = r.choices(
        population=["zip", "repeated", "compressible", "random_mix", "zeros", "ff"],
        weights=[2, 3, 3, 5, 1, 1],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if template == "zip":
        blob = _make_zip_minimal(r)
        # Optionally pad with random mix to allow finds beyond ZIP structures
        if len(blob) < size:
            pad = _mix_patterns(r, size - len(blob))
            blob = blob + pad
        return blob[:4096]

    elif template == "repeated":
        data = _make_repeated_blocks(r, size)
        buf = bytearray(data)
        _insert_needles(r, buf)
        return bytes(buf)

    elif template == "compressible":
        data = _make_highly_compressible(r, size)
        buf = bytearray(data)
        _insert_needles(r, buf)
        return bytes(buf)

    elif template == "random_mix":
        return _mix_patterns(r, size)

    elif template == "zeros":
        buf = bytearray(b"\x00" * size)
        _insert_needles(r, buf)
        return bytes(buf)

    else:  # "ff"
        buf = bytearray(b"\xff" * size)
        _insert_needles(r, buf)
        return bytes(buf)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets many fuzz stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We therefore build a compound buffer that encodes multiple interesting byte sequences
# separated by NULs so the fuzzer can slice/consume them in order.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Minimal local header + file content + central directory + EOCD
# Constructs a valid ZIP with one small file named like the provided filename and stored content.

def build_minimal_zip_stored(file_name: bytes, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Signatures
    LH_SIG = 0x04034B50
    CD_SIG = 0x02014B50
    EOCD_SIG = 0x06054B50

    # DOS time/date: fixed constant (00:00 1980-01-01)
    dos_time = 0
    dos_date = (0 << 9) | (1 << 5) | 1

    fn = file_name
    extra = b""
    comment = b""

    crc = _crc32(content)
    comp_method = 0  # store
    comp_size = len(content)
    uncomp_size = len(content)

    # Local file header
    lh = struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHHIIIHH",
        LH_SIG,      # signature
        20,          # version needed
        0,           # flags
        comp_method, # compression method
        dos_time,
        dos_date,
        crc,
        comp_size,
        uncomp_size,
        len(fn),
        len(extra),
    ) + fn + extra

    local_offset = 0  # start of file in our in-memory buffer
    file_data = content

    # Central directory header for the same file
    external_attr = 0
    internal_attr = 0
    cd = struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII",
        CD_SIG,
        20,          # version made by
        20,          # version needed
        0,           # flags
        comp_method,
        dos_time,
        dos_date,
        crc,
        comp_size,
        uncomp_size,
        len(fn),
        len(extra),
        len(comment),
        0,           # disk number start
        internal_attr,
        external_attr,
        local_offset,
    ) + fn + extra + comment

    # EOCD
    total_entries = 1
    cd_offset = len(lh) + len(file_data)
    cd_size = len(cd)
    eocd = struct.pack(
        "<IHHHHIIH",
        EOCD_SIG,
        0,              # disk number
        0,              # disk number with central dir
        total_entries,
        total_entries,
        cd_size,
        cd_offset,
        len(comment),
    ) + comment

    return lh + file_data + cd + eocd


def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Software CRC32 (poly 0xEDB88320)
    c = 0xFFFFFFFF
    for b in data:
        c ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            mask = -(c & 1)
            c = (c >> 1) ^ (0xEDB88320 & mask)
    return (~c) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-.,:/\\\n\r\t"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def rand_binary(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return rng.randbytes(n)


def interesting_needles(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    needles: List[bytes] = [
        b"\x00", b"\xFF", b"\x00\x00\x00", b"\xFF\xFF",
        b"AAAA", b"BBBB", b"\r\n", b"\n\n", b"END", b"BEGIN",
        b"PK\x03\x04", b"PK\x01\x02",
        b"the", b"The", b"test", b"needle", b"pattern",
    ]
    for _ in range(6):
        needles.append(rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64))
    for _ in range(4):
        needles.append(rand_binary(rng, 1, 32))
    return needles


def interesting_filenames(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    base: List[bytes] = [
        b"/tmp/in.mem",
        b"/tmp/out.mem",
        b"./data.bin",
        b"C:\\temp\\file.bin",
        b"relative/path/file.txt",
        b"../up/dir/archive.zip",
        b"./split.001",
        b"/dev/null",
        b"mem://buffer",
        b"zip://nested.zip",
    ]
    for _ in range(5):
        name = rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20).replace(b" ", b"_")
        base.append(name + b".bin")
    return base


def capped_concat(parts: List[bytes], sep: bytes = b"\x00", cap: int = MAX_TOTAL) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for p in parts:
        if p is None:
            continue
        # allow empty segments to create adjacent NULs
        part = (sep + p) if out else p
        if len(out) + len(part) > cap:
            remaining = cap - len(out)
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            out.extend(part[:remaining])
            break
        out.extend(part)
    return bytes(out)


def build_zip_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    variants: List[bytes] = []
    contents: List[bytes] = [
        b"hello world\n",
        rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64),
        rand_binary(rng, 8, 64),
        b"line 1\nline 2\nline 3\nline 4\nline 5\n",
        b"A" * 128,
        b"B" * 257,
    ]
    for i, payload in enumerate(contents[:4]):
        fn = (b"a" if i == 0 else b"f") + b".txt"
        try:
            z = build_minimal_zip_stored(fn, payload)
            if len(z) <= 1024:
                variants.append(z)
        except Exception:
            continue
    return variants


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Valid ZIP images (small) for mz_zip_reader_open_buffer and writer tests
    parts.extend(build_zip_variants(rng))

    # 2) Filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumption
    for fn in interesting_filenames(rng):
        parts.append(fn)

    # 3) Rich text/binary blobs for read/write and search/find
    lorem = (
        b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. "
        b"Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.\n"
    )
    parts.append(lorem)
    parts.append((b"ABC123\n" * 50)[:600])
    parts.append(bytes(range(0, 256)))
    parts.append(bytes(reversed(range(0, 256))))
    parts.append(rand_binary(rng, 32, 256))
    parts.append(rand_ascii(rng, 16, 200))

    # 4) Search needles of varying sizes
    parts.extend(interesting_needles(rng))

    # 5) Extra field-like small blobs (<= 128)
    for _ in range(4):
        sz = rng.randint(0, 120)
        parts.append(rng.randbytes(sz))

    # 6) Password-like ASCII
    pw_chars = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}:,./?"
    pw_len = rng.randint(4, 32)
    parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(pw_chars) for _ in range(pw_len)))

    # 7) Include an explicit empty segment to allow consumers that expect size==0 cases
    parts.append(b"")

    # Concat all parts with NUL separators, capped to 4096 bytes
    buf = capped_concat(parts, sep=b"\x00", cap=MAX_TOTAL)

    if not buf:
        n = rng.randint(16, 128)
        buf = rng.randbytes(n)

    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid UTF-8, NUL-terminated friendly byte buffers
# intended to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in the target stubs.
#
# Goals:
# - Cover filenames, paths, comments, passwords, wildcards, and general text.
# - Include edge cases: empty-ish, very short, very long (but <= 4096), mixed
#   slashes, dots, Unicode, glob chars, Windows drive roots, zip-specific names, etc.
# - Always valid UTF-8 with no embedded NUL (the harness uses std::string which
#   stores bytes and passes c_str()).
# - Occasionally generate directory-like or file-like paths with extensions.
# - Keep deterministic randomness via the provided seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Some useful Unicode ranges for filenames/comments that are commonly supported
UNICODE_SETS = [
    # ASCII letters, digits and punctuation typical in filenames
    list(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,+!@#%^&()[]{}$=~`'"),
    # Latin-1 supplement (no control chars)
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x00A1, 0x017F)],
    # Greek
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x0370, 0x03FF)],
    # Cyrillic
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x0400, 0x04FF)],
    # CJK (a small sample range to keep sizes reasonable)
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x4e00, 0x4e00 + 512)],
    # Emojis (basic range subset)
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x1F600, 0x1F64F)],
]

# Common directory and file name components
EXTS = ["txt", "bin", "dat", "zip", "gz", "csv", "json", "xml", "png", "jpg", "dll", "so"]
DIR_NAMES = [
    "tmp", "Temp", "cache", "Cache", "data", "logs", "ホーム", "Документы", "数据", "テスト",
    "Δεδομένα", "工作", "build", "release", "._hidden", ".config", "用户", "用户资料"
]
BASENAMES = [
    "README", "notes", "报告", "テスト", "file", "data", "archive", "backup", "résumé", "Στοιχεία",
    "данные", "資料", "emoji_😀", "long-name-with-dashes", "a", "abc", "NULfree"
]
WILDCARDS = ["*", "?", "[a-z]", "**", "*.zip", "*.?", "file*", "??.dat", "[!0-9]*.txt"]

# Path templates to exercise different join/resolve behaviors
PATH_PATTERNS = [
    "{base}.{ext}",
    "{dir}/{base}.{ext}",
    "{dir1}/{dir2}/{base}.{ext}",
    "./{base}",
    "../{dir}/{base}.{ext}",
    "{dir1}\\{dir2}\\{base}.{ext}",  # Windows-style
    "/{dir}/{base}",                    # absolute POSIX
    "C:\\{dir}\\{base}.{ext}",        # Windows drive
    "//server/share/{dir}/{base}.{ext}",
    "{dir}/.hidden/{base}.{ext}",
]

# Comment/password specific patterns
COMMENT_SNIPPETS = [
    "This is a test archive comment.",
    "こんにちは世界", "Привет мир", "Hola mundo", "مرحبا بالعالم", "😀 UTF-8 ok",
    "Path: ../relative/./x", "Use * and ? wildcards", "a" * 100, "Edge—case—dashes",
]
PASSWORD_WORDS = [
    "", "password", "123456", "letmein", "pässwörd", "秘密", "пароль", "😀😀😀",
    "with spaces", "UPPERlower123", "!@#$%^&*()_+", "verylong" + "x" * 64,
]

# Ensure strings are valid for C-string use (no embedded NUL) and bounded
def sanitize(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]):
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]

def rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    # Mix multiple sets for diversity
    out = []
    for _ in range(count):
        set_idx = rng.randrange(len(UNICODE_SETS) + 2)
        if set_idx < len(UNICODE_SETS):
            out.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SETS[set_idx]))
        else:
            # fallback ASCII safe
            out.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"))
    return "".join(out)

def make_filename(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Build a plausible filename/path
    dir1 = rand_choice(rng, DIR_NAMES)
    dir2 = rand_choice(rng, DIR_NAMES)
    base = rand_choice(rng, BASENAMES)
    # Randomly add unicode to base
    base += rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(0, 6))
    ext = rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
    pattern = rand_choice(rng, PATH_PATTERNS)
    s = pattern.format(dir=dir1, dir1=dir1, dir2=dir2, base=base, ext=ext)
    # Sometimes add wildcard or normalize slashes cases
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + ("/" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "\\")
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s.replace("/", "\\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "/")
    # Limit length and ensure no NUL
    return sanitize(s, max_len)

def make_comment(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    parts = [rand_choice(rng, COMMENT_SNIPPETS)]
    # Optionally add more text and unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(" ")
        parts.append(rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(5, 40)))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(" ")
        parts.append(rand_choice(rng, WILDCARDS))
    return sanitize("".join(parts), max_len)

def make_password(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = rand_choice(rng, PASSWORD_WORDS)
    else:
        s = rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(6, 24))
    return sanitize(s, max_len)

def make_wildcard(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    base = rand_choice(rng, WILDCARDS)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = base + "/" + rand_choice(rng, WILDCARDS)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = "**/" + base
    return sanitize(base, max_len)

def make_path_op_string(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Good for mz_path_* APIs
    options = []
    options.append(make_filename(rng, max_len))
    options.append(make_wildcard(rng, max_len))
    options.append("." * rng.randint(1, 3) + "/" + make_filename(rng, max_len - 4))
    options.append("../" * rng.randint(1, 3) + make_filename(rng, max_len - 6))
    options.append("/" + make_filename(rng, max_len - 1))
    options.append("C:/" + make_filename(rng, max_len - 3))
    s = rand_choice(rng, options)
    return sanitize(s, max_len)

def assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Build a small set of candidate strings; harness will pick per-call
    items: List[str] = []

    # Filenames/paths
    for _ in range(6):
        items.append(make_filename(rng, 512))

    # Comments (zip global/comment per entry)
    for _ in range(4):
        items.append(make_comment(rng, 1024))

    # Passwords
    for _ in range(4):
        items.append(make_password(rng, 128))

    # Wildcards and path patterns
    for _ in range(6):
        items.append(make_path_op_string(rng, 512))

    # A few extremes: very short, very long (still < 4096)
    items.append("a")
    items.append("/")
    items.append("..")
    items.append("*.*")
    items.append("\\\\?\\C:\\very\\long\\path\\with\\backslashes\\and space.txt")
    long_text = make_comment(rng, 3500)
    items.append(long_text)

    # Ensure all are valid UTF-8 (Python str) and convert to bytes (UTF-8) without NULs
    out: List[bytes] = []
    for s in items:
        s = sanitize(s, MAX_SIZE - 1)  # keep room if concatenated by harness; but std::string doesn't need NUL
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        out.append(b)
    return out

def pack_multi(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Combine multiple strings into one buffer with separators; the fuzzer infra
    # typically slices per-call, but when given as an initial buffer it may use
    # tokens. Use line breaks to separate to be human-inspectable too.
    sep = b"\n"
    # Ensure final size <= MAX_SIZE
    result = sep.join(strings)
    if len(result) > MAX_SIZE:
        result = result[:MAX_SIZE]
        # Avoid cutting in middle of UTF-8 sequence: backtrack to valid boundary
        # UTF-8 continuation bytes are 0b10xxxxxx (0x80-0xBF).
        i = len(result) - 1
        while i >= 0 and (result[i] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            i -= 1
        if i >= 0:
            result = result[:i+1]
    return result


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = assemble_corpus(rng)
    rng.shuffle(corpus)
    return pack_multi(corpus)
